findings.issue_text: **`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11`** — `execute(...)[0]['id']` will raise (`IndexError`/`NoMethodError`) whenever no row named `embed_category` exists in `site_settings`, which is the common case since `embed_category` defaults to `''` and most installations never override it. This means `rake db:migrate` will crash for essentially every site that hasn't customized embedding, blocking the upgrade entirely. Fix: guard the result before indexing, e.g. `result = execute(...); category_id = result.count > 0 ? result[0]['id'].to_i : 0`, mirroring the `cmd_tuples > 0` check already used a few lines later for `embeddable_hosts`.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17`** — `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` compares the DB's lower-cased `host` column against a non-lower-cased `host` variable (the value extracted from `URI(...).host`). If a referer/URL ever has a mixed-case hostname, the match silently fails even though the host is legitimately registered. Fix: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6-7`** — `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally. If `host` is blank/nil (e.g., the admin API is hit with `embeddable_host[host]` empty/missing, bypassing only the client-side `cantSave` guard), this raises `NoMethodError` instead of failing the `validates_format_of` check gracefully, turning a normal validation failure into a 500. Fix: `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...).sub(...)` or short-circuit when `host.blank?`.

**`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-17`** — `update`/`destroy` fetch via `.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil-check; a missing/already-deleted id causes `NoMethodError` on `host.host=`/`host.destroy` (500) instead of a clean error. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (which Discourse's standard `rescue_from RecordNotFound` typically turns into a 404) or explicitly guard for `nil`.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`** — no uniqueness constraint (model validation or DB index) on `host`. Two rows can be created for the same hostname pointing at different categories; `record_for_host`'s unscoped `.first` then makes the resulting category assignment/access decision nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` plus a unique index in the migration.

**Test coverage is superficial for the feature's core logic.** `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert `< Admin::AdminController` — there is no test exercising `create`/`update`/`destroy` success or failure paths, the uncategorized-category fallback, or error rendering. There is also no `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` at all for the new model, despite it containing the validation, the host-normalization callback, and the two methods (`record_for_host`, `host_allowed?`) that gate embed access — the security-relevant logic is only indirectly exercised via `embed_controller_spec.rb`. Given the migration bug above, a data-migration test would also have caught that regression.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:4-6`** and the corresponding `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` route — the `saveChanges` action is never invoked from `embedding.hbs` (grepped the whole JS tree, no other reference). Even if wired up, the controller action doesn't consume any request params, so it would be a no-op round trip. This looks like leftover scaffolding; either remove it or wire up a real "Save" affordance.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`** — `delete()`'s `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save()`. A failed delete fails silently with no user feedback.

**Fabricator files were swapped.** `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `category`/`diff_category`/`happy_category`/`private_category` fabricators. Functionally harmless (Fabrication loads every file in the directory regardless of name) but clearly an accidental rename/swap that will confuse the next person looking for the category fabricator.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2`** — the format regex `\.[a-z]{2,5}` rejects TLDs longer than 5 characters (`.technology`, `.international`, etc.), unnecessarily restricting valid hostnames admins can register.

**`app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb`** / **`embedding_serializer.rb`** — the explicit `id`/`host`/`category_id` methods just proxy to `object.<attr>`, identical to `ActiveModel::Serializer`'s default `attributes` behavior; can be deleted.

**`db/migrate/...rb:24`** — the data-carryover `INSERT` builds SQL via raw string interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) rather than quoting/binding. Low risk since values originate from previously-admin-entered site settings, but a hostname containing a single quote would break the migration.

Removing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, `embed_category`, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` outright (`app/models/site_setting.rb`, `config/site_settings.yml`) is a breaking API change for any theme/plugin referencing them, with no deprecation shim — worth a changelog/upgrade note even if acceptable for this codebase's usual practice.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

That makes category assignment and access checks potentially inconsistent. Adding a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique DB index would address this.

The only persistence shown is per-row via `embeddable-host` -> `host.save(props)` hitting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`. Separately, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (wired to `PUT /admin/customize/embedding`) ignores request params and simply re-renders the same serialized embedding object, making any `embedding.update({})` call a no-op round trip. So the finding that this looks like unused/leftover scaffolding is directly verifiable from the diff.

Since `destroyRecord()` returns a promise that can reject (e.g., network/server error), this omission means a failed delete will not trigger `popupAjaxError` and provides no explicit user-facing error handling in this code path.

Since `h` comes from `site_settings.value` (split by newlines) and is inserted without quoting/escaping, a hostname containing a single quote would produce invalid SQL and break the migration. This is a concrete correctness defect visible in the diff (and also implies potential SQL injection if the stored setting were tampered with).

Any external code (plugins/themes/custom scripts) that references these settings/method will now raise errors or see missing settings at runtime, with no compatibility shim or deprecation path shown in the diff.
